title: Precision usage accounting for embeddings, reranker and function-call signatures
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
We are seeing several classes of billing and quota anomalies for non-chat endpoints (embeddings, rerank, and structured function-call outputs). Symptoms include: inconsistent token/usage attribution when a request triggers tool calls or returns structured JSON blobs; duplicate counting between pre- and post-processing pipelines (embedding batching + reranker scoring); and rate-limit enforcement that treats tool-calls as separate request categories, leading to unexpected quota exhaustion for customers using hybrid flows.

Goals:
- Produce a single source-of-truth metering pipeline for non-chat flows that accurately attributes chargeable units (embedding vectors, reranker scoring tokens, function-call output tokens, and structured output size).
- Ensure rate limits and quotas reflect combined usage across the whole request lifecycle (ingress parsing -> model inference -> tool-call execution -> response serialization).
- Provide retroactive reconciliation for affected customers and guardrails to prevent future misbilling.

Scope and assumptions:
- Focus on embeddings, reranker endpoints, and non-chat structured outputs (including function-calling where an LLM returns a structured call payload). Chat endpoints have separate accounting and are out of scope for this ticket.
- We will not change pricing tiers in this work; we will fix counting and quota enforcement to match existing pricing rules.

Planned approach:
1) Instrumentation: add canonical usage events at these boundaries: request-received, pre-tokenization, model-inference-start, model-inference-end, tool-call-invocation, tool-call-completion, response-serialized. Each event will emit a compact canonical record (unit, unit_type, request_id, model_variant, sequence_length, vector_count, serialized_bytes).
2) Centralize metering: route canonical records to the billing ingestion service (billing-ingest-v2). This avoids ad-hoc counters in multiple services (embedder, reranker, tool-proxy).
3) Quota enforcement: update quota-check logic to consult the canonical event stream (or a pre-aggregated fast path) so quota decisions include pending tool-call units until completion (pre-reserve tokens to avoid race conditions).
4) Reconciliation: run a backfill job to reconcile last 90 days of events and produce correction documents for any customers with >0.5% discrepancy. Coordinate finance for credits/refunds and customer communications.
5) Testing and rollout: add unit/integration tests, synthetic load tests covering edge cases (tool-call chains, multi-vector embeddings, nested structured results), staged rollout with feature flag and customer opt-in.

Trade-offs / alternatives considered:
- Option A: Incremental per-service fixes — faster but brittle and duplicates logic.
- Option B (chosen): Centralize canonical events — more initial work but safer long-term and enables simpler audits.

Open decisions / blockers:
- How to pre-reserve quota for tool-calls that may spawn additional model calls (recursive tool-calls). Proposal: conservative pre-reserve based on configured upper bound per integration. (Jin to draft limits by 2026-03-10).
- Finance acceptance criteria for issuing customer credits vs. account adjustments. (PM/Finance sync scheduled).
- SAML/KMS logging constraints for Private deployments when exporting events to billing ingestion.

Risks:
- Short-term increased latency for quota checks if the pre-aggregation path misbehaves. Mitigation: keep fast-path cache with TTL 5s.
- Complexity in migrating historical invoices if backfill finds large discrepancies. Mitigation: cap retrospective credits and coordinate CS/Finance.

Success metrics:
- Metering discrepancy between service logs and billing ledger drops below 0.02% across sampled requests for a week.
- No new customer-reported billing anomalies for non-chat endpoints in 30 days post rollout.
- Quota enforcement false positives under 0.1%.

Operational runbook excerpts (for incidents):
- If duplicate-counting spike detected: enable billing-ingest-v1 fallback and pause backfill jobs.
- If quota over-enforcement observed: rollback fast-path to cached allowances and open emergency flag to exempt affected customer keys.

Longer term follow-ups (separate tickets):
- Expose detailed per-route usage breakdown in Console for embedded/rerank flows.
- Rate-limiter UI to show pending tool-call reservations.
comments: 2026-02-28: Created ticket after postmortem of billing variance incident (see linked incident doc). Reporting observed 0.8% overcharge on embedding-heavy accounts.

2026-03-02: Spike analysis: root cause narrowed to double-counting in the pre-tokenizer hook and the embedder service when requests use batched embeddings + reranker pipeline. Jin started prototype for canonical events.
2026-03-05: Design review with PM (Samir Gupta) and Finance. Decided on central events pipeline (billing-ingest-v2). PM asked for clear rollback and customer communication plan.

2026-03-08: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/214 (billing-ingest-v2 schema + ingest adapter). Initial review comments from Monica: require end-to-end test vectors and schema versioning. Assigned to Jin.

2026-03-11: Integration test added that simulates tool-call that returns structured JSON with 3 nested arrays — validated correct vector_count and serialized_bytes attribution. Failure case found: tool-proxy omitted model_variant. Patch merged.
2026-03-13: Started backfill dry run on staging for last 30 days; found 12 customers with >1% discrepancy. Finance notified to prepare manual review table.
